problem: The bullet says 'not every validator waits to its own random time and then races'. That contradicts how PoET actually works: every validator draws a random wait and sleeps for it; the one whose wait ends first (the smallest W) wakes first and proposes, while the rest are still waiting and then verify the proof. A student who learns this bullet will believe only the winner waits, which is the wrong model.
fix: In PoET every validator draws a random wait and sleeps for it. The validator whose wait ends first, that is, the one with the smallest W, proposes; the others are still waiting and then verify its signed wait proof. There is no simultaneous race to propose, because the shortest wait always finishes first.

problem: The formula defines proposer(n), n, N, T and mod, but never says what start(n) means or where time zero is. A reader cannot tell whether start(n) is the slot's beginning time in seconds from chain start.
fix: Add to the where-list: start(n) is the time in seconds at which slot n begins, measured from the start of slot 1, so slot 1 begins at 0 s.
